#### What this PR does / why we need it:
- Introduce PassiveRateLimiter which implements all methods of previous RateLimiter except Accept() and Wait()
- Change RateLimiter interface to extend PassiveRateLimiter by additionally implementing Accept() and Wait()
- Make client-go/tools/record use PassiveRateLimiter

Refactor EventSourceObjectSpamFilter, EventAggregator, EventCorrelator

- EventSourceObjectSpamFilter, EventAggregator, EventCorrelator use clock.PassiveClock now.
	- This won't be a breaking change because even if a clock.Clock is passed, it still implements the clock.PassiveClock interface.
- Extend clock.PassiveClock through Clock.
- Replace pacakge local implementation of realClock with clock.RealClock
- In flowcontrol/throttle.go split tokenBucketRateLimiters to use Clock and clock.PassiveClock.
- Migrate client-go/tools/record tests from using IntervalClock to using SimpleIntervalClock (honest implementation of clock.PassiveClock)

pr_comments:
This is a good start.

We should be able to refactor further, so that a `EventSourceObjectSpamFilter` has a `PassiveClock` rather than a `Clock`, and `NewTokenBucketPassiveRateLimiterWithClock` takes a `PassiveClock` rather than a `Clock`.  That would enable us to replace the use of `IntervalClock` with `SimpleIntervalClock`.

@MikeSpreitzer, in order to move from `IntervalClock` to `SimpleIntervalClock`, the clocks in events.go also needed to be changed. I went through the code and found that the only method of clock being used is `Now()`, which the `PassiveClock` provides. I've made the change of migrating that to `PassiveClock` as well. This won't be breaking because any clock that implements `clock.Clock` will also implement `clock.PassiveClock`.

issue_context.title: client-go/tools/record/ tests use IntervalClock
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:
While cleaning up the divergence in clock packages it came to my attention that many methods of IntervalClock panic.  In fact, IntervalClock is an honest implementation of only PassiveClock, not the full Clock interface.  In k8s.io/utils/clock/testing we now have SimpleIntervalClock, which statically implements only PassiveClock and does so without any panics.  So I went looking for uses of IntervalClock, intending to replace them with uses of SimpleIntervalClock so that our code base is more obviously correct.

The only uses of IntervalClock that I found in k/k are in the unit tests in client-go/tools/record.  However, one cannot simply substitute in SimpleIntervalClock for IntervalClock!  The problem is that `EventSourceObjectSpamFilter::Filter` invokes `flowcontrol.NewTokenBucketRateLimiterWithClock(f.qps, f.burst, f.clock)`, and that rate limiter has code that invokes the clock's `Sleep` method (which panics, in the case of IntervalClock).  The test passes because no code in client-go/tools/record invokes the Accept method of the rate limiter (which is the only place where the rate limiter invokes the clock's Sleep method).

I can think of two approaches to fixing this problem.  One is to rewrite the tests in client-go/tools/record to use a clock that does not panic.  The other approach is to factor the rate limiters, so that there is: (1) a `PassiveRateLimiter` interface that lacks the `Accept` method, and (2) the full RateLimiter interface, which extends `PassiveRateLimiter` by adding the `Accept` method.

#### What you expected to happen:
I expected to be able to eliminate uses of a type with many methods that just panic.
